comment: [SOURCE] Transcribed from 'GAYK/DOYLE Ram Training Program Waiver of Liability & Checklist' (GAYK
North America, doc 240916). The liability paragraph and the acknowledgement line are VERBATIM —
they are the legally operative text and are pinned byte-exact by required-content.json. All ten
topics keep their source numbering, titles and descriptions.
[WHY THIS IS NOT AN equipment-preinspection VARIANT] It is a signed ACKNOWLEDGEMENT that training
was delivered and liability accepted — not a machine condition check. It carries no pass/fail
scale, produces no defect record, and is signed once per training delivery rather than once per
shift. Filing it under the inspection parent would put a legal waiver into the Equipment Check
Sheets Box category (intake.PORTAL_FORM_CATEGORY) and into daily-inspection reporting. It gets its
own parent, the Visitor Sign-In / Toolbox Talk precedent for a form whose output is signatures
rather than findings.
[NULL VARIANT, MANUFACTURER-SCOPED IDENTITY] This shipped first as a variant ('GAYK/DOYLE Ram')
to future-proof for a second manufacturer, and tests/test_form_catalog.py
::test_single_form_parent_is_null_variant correctly rejected it: registry.ts formCatalog()
branches BINARY on variant_label, so a lone form carrying one renders a degenerate one-option 3rd
picklist the PM must click through on every single submission — a real daily cost paid for a
hypothetical second machine. So variant_label is null. The IDENTITY still carries '-gayk-ram'
(unlike jha / visitor-sign-in, where identity == parent) precisely so the future case is cheap:
adding a second manufacturer means a new sibling definition plus setting a variant_label on both
catalog rows in the same edit — never renaming an identity, which would strand filed submissions.
[SIGN-OFF SHAPE] The source prints ONE signature block (Signature / Printed Name and Title /
Company / Date). It is modeled as a signature_table with min_rows 1 + allow_add, NOT a header:
min_rows 1 keeps the source's single-signer default, while allow_add lets one training delivery
to a crew record every attendee — each with their own printed name, title and company beside their
own signature, which is what a per-person liability acceptance requires. This is the
toolbox-talk-*-v1 sign-in precedent. The source's 'Date' rides the work_date envelope.
[TOPIC CONTENT] The ten topics are content_blocks (static, non-editable), not checklist items:
the source is a record that GAYK PROVIDED this information, not a list the signer ticks off. There
are no checkboxes on the source page. The header sentence 'GAYK has provided the information
regarding the following topics: Operation and Maintenance' is preserved as the section title's
lead block so the topics are never read as duties owed by the signer.

branding.title: GAYK/DOYLE Ram Training Program — Waiver of Liability & Checklist

sections.text: As is true of all construction equipment, operating the Machine involves inherent risk of personal injury, including death, and property damage. Although GAYK endeavors to demonstrate precautions for mitigating these risks, they cannot be eliminated entirely. The sole responsibility for any injuries or damages suffered are accepted by the customer, and the customer agrees that GAYK N.A. LLC, and its representatives, shall be held harmless from any and all liability arising from the use or operation of the equipment.

blocks.body: GAYK has provided the information regarding the following topics: Operation and Maintenance

blocks.heading: 1. Pre-Start-Up Walk Around and Fluid Levels
blocks.body: Checking vital fluids (including engine oil, hydraulic oil and fuel levels) and inspection of the Machine prior to operation.

blocks.heading: 2. Rotation
blocks.body: Rotating the Machine on its chassis before attempting to raise the mast

blocks.heading: 3. Electrical Components
blocks.body: Discussion of the operation of the electrical components, including the ignition switch, work lights (if any), and safety light (orange beacon)

blocks.heading: 4. Ignition & Cycling
blocks.body: Starting the Machine and cycling from idle to operational rpm

blocks.heading: 6. Driving
blocks.body: Discussion of how to drive the Machine, including steering, maneuvering, visibility, and Machine stability

blocks.heading: 7. Mast Operation
blocks.body: Raising and lowering the mast and centering the leveling "bubble"

blocks.heading: 8. Hammer Operation
blocks.body: Operating the hammer and turning on the pile driver

blocks.heading: 10. Grease Points
blocks.body: Demonstrating the correct grease points on the Machine and hammer and discussing frequency of required greasing

sections.text: I have read, understand and agree to the matters covered in this document.
